away.name: Casey DeSmith
away.news: DeSmith won a career-high 15 games last season and emerged as one of the NHL's most reliable backup goalies, but he has been used sparingly to start the 2026-27 season. That said, the 35-year-old DeSmith was stellar in his most recent outing, saving 25 of 26 shots (.962 SV%) in a 2-1 overtime win over the Florida Panthers. home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer has emerged as the undisputed number-one goalie in St. Louis and has been consistent on most nights. The 26-year-old goalie has had an outstanding November, posting a 2.20 GAA and .925 SV% in eight games (4-3-1). The Blues enter Friday's game as +111 home underdogs against the Dallas Stars.

away.name: Linus Ullmark
away.news: Ullmark has been outstanding this season, but is coming off his worst performance so far, allowing four goals on 31 shots (.871 SV%) in a 5-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. Despite the recent blip, the 33-year-old Swedish goalie is still sporting an absurd 1.63 GAA and .935 SV% in 14 games (12-2-0). The Senators enter Friday's game as +135 road underdogs against the Tampa Bay Lightning.

home.name: Dennis Hildeby
home.news: Hildeby has been used sparingly this season but has been reliable on most nights, winning four of six outings (4-1-1). Tampa Bay enters Friday’s game as -132 home favourites against the Ottawa Senators.

away.name: Leevi Merilainen

home.name: Dan Vladar
home.news: The Flyers have relied a bit more heavily on Joseph Woll in recent weeks, but he is coming off a poor performance, so they will revert to Vladar on Friday. The Flyers enter Friday's game as sizeable -225 home favourites against the Vancouver Canucks.

away.name: Jacob Markstrom
away.news: Markstrom hasn't had to be spectacular this season, but he has done enough on most nights to help his team secure victories. home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Over the past two seasons, Thompson quietly became one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. The Capitals enter Friday's game as slight -101 home underdogs against the Florida Panthers.

away.name: John Gibson
away.news: The Red Wings have relied, deservedly so, on Daniil Tarasov in recent weeks, but they will turn to Gibson on Friday. He has allowed three or more goals in 11 of his last 13 games (4-8-1). The Red Wings enter Friday's contest as +115 road underdogs against the Columbus Blue Jackets.

home.name: Jet Greaves
home.news: Greaves hasn't played much in recent weeks, but will return to the crease on Friday. Greaves has lost eight of 10 starts this season (2-8-0) while allowing a concerning three or more goals eight times. The Blue Jackets enter Friday's game as -125 home favourites against a Detroit Red Wings team coming off a 5-1 win over the Vancouver Canucks.

away.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
away.news: Scott Wedgewood recorded a shutout in his most recent game, arguably his first strong performance of the season, but in consecutive games since, Colorado will return to Blackwood, who has been their go-to guy all season. The Avalanche enter Friday's game as slight +102 road underdogs against the Minnesota Wild.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Filip Gustavsson returned earlier this week, but the team seems comfortable continuing to lean on Wallstedt, who has deservedly been the NHL's busiest goalie this season. Minnesota enters Friday's game as slight -112 home favourites against the Colorado Avalanche.

away.name: Darcy Kuemper
away.news: Kuemper has been far from stellar this season, but through 22 games, he remains the only goalie with a win for the Kings. That said, the 36-year-old veteran goalie saved 29 of 30 shots (.967 SV%) in his most recent game, a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens. He has won three straight games while saving 82 of 86 shots (.953 SV%). The Kings enter Friday's game as slight -113 road favourites against the Anaheim Ducks.

home.name: Laurent Brossoit
home.news: Brossoit had a successful stint with the Ducks earlier this month, but was surprisingly sent down to San Diego (AHL) after a 4-2 loss to the Nashville Predators on November 11th, when he allowed four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%). In his return to action on Wednesday, Brossoit made a strong case for staying in the NHL, recording the Ducks' first shutout of the season with 23 saves in a 7-0 win over the San Jose Sharks. The Ducks enter Friday's game as slight -104 home underdogs against the Los Angeles Kings, who are coming off a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens.

away.name: Carter Hart
away.news: Hart has won four of his last five (4-1-0) but has been far from stellar, allowing three or more goals in four of those games. The Golden Knights enter Friday’s game as sizeable -206 road favourites against the San Jose Sharks.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov was serviceable in his most recent game, saving 26 of 29 shots (.897 SV%), but his team fell to a 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild. In his last 14 games, Askarov has played much better than his 4-7-1 record suggests, posting a 2.97 GAA and .903 SV%. The Sharks enter Friday's game as +179 home underdogs against the Vegas Golden Knights.

away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Despite losing 5-2 to the Carolina Hurricanes in his most recent outing, Garand was solid, saving 36 of 40 shots (.900 SV%). The Rangers enter Friday's game as -178 road favourites against the Chicago Blackhawks.

home.name: Semyon Varlamov
home.news: After missing the entire 2025-26 season due to an injury, Varlamov's return to the crease in 2026-27 has been inconsistent. That said, he has helped his team record a point in six of his last seven games (2-1-3). The Islanders enter Friday's game as -117 home favourites in a rematch against the Jets, who are 9-1-1 in their past 11 games.

away.name: Sergei Murashov
away.news: The Penguins are having a miserable season, but the lightly used Murashov has shown some encouraging signs between the pipes. The loss ended a solid three-game stretch for Murashov (2-1-0), in which he saved 91 of 98 shots (.929 SV%). The Penguins enter Friday's game as +126 road underdogs against the Buffalo Sabres.

away.name: Philipp Grubauer
away.news: Grubauer has had ups and downs in the 2026-27 season and is coming off a poor performance, allowing four goals on 28 shots (.857 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the San Jose Sharks. home.name: Tristan Jarry
home.news: After a disappointing introduction to the Oilers in the 2025-26 season, Jarry has been reliable on most nights in 2026-27. It snapped a six-game stretch in which Jarry allowed three or fewer goals in each game (4-0-2). The Oilers enter Friday's outing as -203 home favourites against the Seattle Kraken, who are coming off a 3-1 loss to the Chicago Blackhawks.
